outcome: Neonatal intensive care unit/special care nursery admissions
cohort: 10,133 women with term breech singleton pregnancies in New South Wales, Australia, from 2009 to 2012, of whom 5,197 were classified as eligible for vaginal breech delivery
finding: In a population of women considered eligible for vaginal breech birth, intended vaginal delivery was associated with higher rates of neonatal morbidity compared to planned cesarean section.
mod_finding: Intended vaginal breech delivery was associated with higher rates of neonatal morbidity (6.0% vs 2.1%), neonatal birth trauma (7.4% vs 0.9%), Apgar <4 at one minute (10.5% vs 1.1%), Apgar <7 at five minutes (4.3% vs 0.5%) and neonatal intensive care unit/special care nursery admissions (16.2% vs 6.6%) than planned cesarean section.
